analysis.title: Global Economics Year Ahead 2027: License to chip – shaken not stirred
key_insights: Base case is global growth of 3.4% in 2027 vs 3.5% in 2026, with global inflation easing only from 3.1% to 2.9%. The view is cautiously constructive and assumes the AI capex cycle continues and Iran does not escalate massively.

The AI narrative creates a binary outlook: resilient growth if it holds, a global slowdown if it collapses. A confidence shock hitting US equities could hit US consumption and capex and reverse Asia's tech export cycle.
The US keeps outpacing other developed economies at 2.3% growth in 2027 (4Q/4Q 2.2%). AI capex should stay strong through at least 1H27 and slow from late 2027, and the consumer is the second pillar.

BofA's Fed call may be the most aggressive on the sell side: three more 25bp hikes in Dec, Jan and Mar to 4.50-4.75%, with no cuts. Core PCE ends 2027 at 2.6% and risks tilt toward more hikes, potentially 5% or beyond if wages inflect higher.

The Fed path hinges on 1H27 base effects. Core PCE ran 3.9% annualized Dec '25 to May '26, so a sharp y/y decline could delay a Mar '27 hike, while large 1Q27 price resets would put super-sized hikes in play.

The Euro area is the weakest link at 0.8% growth in 2027, below consensus. France is forecast at -0.1% with a technical recession and Italy at 0.3%. The ECB makes a final hike in Dec 2026, then cuts from Sep-27 to a 1.5% deposit rate in 2028, earlier and deeper than consensus.

China slows from 4.6% in 2026 to 4.2% in 2027 and 4.0% in 2028, below consensus, with CPI at 0.7%. Net exports carry growth, policy support stays broadly flat, no PBoC rate or RRR cuts are expected in 2027, and China keeps exporting goods deflation.

Japan: the BoJ is expected to hike three more times (Dec, Mar, Jul) to 2%, above market pricing of two hikes by summer. Peak CPI is raised to 3.8% y/y before the April food tax cut, and 2027 growth is 0.7%.

UK: above consensus on growth (1.5% vs 1.2%) and inflation (3.8% vs 3.2%). BoE hikes in Dec and Mar to a 4.50% peak, vs consensus 4.25%. Market pricing of about five total hikes is called excessive, and cuts come in 2028 to 3.5%.

Other DM central banks: the SNB stays on hold at 0% against two hikes priced. The RBA holds 4.85% through most of 2027 and cuts from 4Q27. The RBNZ hikes to 3% in Dec then holds, 35-50bp below the market. The BoC hikes in Jan to 2.75% and again later. Riksbank hikes once more in Feb, and Norges Bank is done at 4.5%.

EM Asia: Korea and Taiwan are key beneficiaries of the AI export boom, with Asia tech exports up 67% y/y. Korea is forecast at 3.9% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027, with a current account surplus above 21% of GDP versus consensus 16-17%. India is above consensus at 7.4% CY27 with 75bp more RBI hikes.

LatAm: Brazil is below consensus at 0.3% GDP in 2027, Selic 13.25% at end-27 vs 12.75% consensus, and holds until 4Q27 amid fiscal stress after Lula's win. Mexico is above consensus at 2.2% on an AI-related export boom. Colombia, Peru and Argentina are more constructive than consensus.

EEMEA: growth rebounds from this year's energy shock, with a Gulf oil price war possible post-ceasefire and an OPEC+ meeting on 29 Nov. The CBRT is less dovish than consensus, with a 31% policy rate at end-27 vs 28% consensus. Israel, South Africa and the CEE fiscal divide are covered, with hikes in Czechia and Poland.

Real rates and fiscal risk: long-end Treasury yields are back above 5%, deficits are much larger than pre-GFC, and AI capex is increasingly debt-financed. A bond buyers' strike or bond vigilantism is flagged as a risk, and tighter financial conditions hit Europe and EM harder than the US.

Geopolitics: the Iran conflict is far from over and the energy price floor rises after each spike. The Democratic midterm win lowers escalation risk at the margin, but BofA expects no swift resolution. Nvidia chip-diversion reports could trigger US export controls and Chinese rare-earth controls.
2027 elections are a risk calendar: France (presidential Apr/May, the biggest systemic risk for the Euro area), Italy 2H27, Argentina Oct 2027, Mexico midterms Jun 2027, Nigeria Jan 2027.

sector_views.rationale: AI capex and chip export prices drive the strongest growth in EM Asia, with a tech upcycle still having legs through 2027.
Energy shock, tight financial conditions and fiscal constraints keep growth at 0.8%, with France in technical recession.

earnings_insights: Hyperscaler capex is on track for about $720bn in 2026, roughly triple the 2024 level, with backlog/RPO above $2.5tn per BofA US equity analysts (estimate, not a reported print).

risk_factors: Implosion of the AI narrative causing an equity correction and negative wealth effects.
Sharp rise in global real rates and bond vigilantism, with long-end Treasury yields above 5%.
Renewed Iran escalation or US-China tech and rare-earth escalation as a stagflationary supply shock.
Fiscal deficits unaddressed in the US, France, UK and Japan.
El Niño food and inflation pressures, and election surprises in France, Italy and Argentina.

tension_points.bull_case: AI capex stays strong through at least 1H27, with winner-takes-all rational overinvestment and hyperscaler backlog above $2.5tn supporting growth.
tension_points.bear_case: A monetization shortfall could trigger a market correction hitting US consumption and Asian tech exports, and AI-related components have grown about 26% annualized, suggesting a front-loaded wave.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A loss of confidence in AI monetization or a sharp capex guide-down that triggers a sizable US equity correction.

tension_points.bull_case: Sticky core inflation and strong demand justify hikes in Dec, Jan and Mar to 4.50-4.75%, with risks of more.
tension_points.bear_case: A sharp decline in y/y core PCE as 1H26 prints are lapped could take the Mar '27 hike off the table or delay it.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp decline in core PCE y/y as the 3.9% annualized Dec '25 to May '26 prints roll off.
